rv.q: Packed with laughs, original songs, and royal hijinks, this new musical is something like Shakespeare meets Spaceballs meets The Emperor’s New Clothes.
In the longueurs, though, I fancied myself like the titular monarch, casting judgement on a show that had royally squandered its potential.
It is weirdly out of place in this ragtag romp that wants to be Once Upon a Mattress crossed with Something Rotten! , with maybe a touch of A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to Forum .
But try as they might (and they try so hard) the writers never strike comedic gold, suffering from a deadly combination of unsharpened tools and poor aim.
Nevertheless, the musical is loads of fun, with a cast that gives 110% throughout.
There’s a good deal of talent wasted on this unruly royal mess of a show.
At its best, comedy does more than amuse: it makes us think.
We’re happy, too, to absorb his enthusiasm, while enduring the hyperactive overreach of a production that was surely rushed to the stage while still a work-in-progress.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this Renaissance-set musical comedy, with most finding it overlong and self-indulgent, though its cast and insider theater humor earn some praise. Theater devotees may enjoy it most.

vr.q: It's incredibly lazy writing, and frankly, musical theatre deserves better.
